name: Lake Kawaguchiko
tagline: Kai country at the foot of Fuji: thick noodles in miso, and a hard udon from a textile town.
history: Kawaguchiko is in the old province of Kai (Yamanashi), Takeda Shingen's land. Rice grew poorly, and when silkworm farming turned paddies into mulberry fields, winter wheat became the staple. Hence hōtō: thick, flat noodles with no salt in the dough that go raw straight into the miso pot, thickening the broth along with the pumpkin as it breaks down.

The story goes that Shingen cut the ingredients with his sword, but Japanese Wikipedia treats that as post-war tourist folklore. The name probably comes from 餺飥 (hakutaku), a noodle dish cited in Heian-era dictionaries.

Next door in Fujiyoshida, the everyday food is Yoshida udon. In the silk-weaving town the women wove and the men cooked a hard, filling udon so they could eat without stopping work. It also fed the Fuji pilgrims. Today there are over 60 shops, almost all lunch-only, many in family homes.
winter: Winter is hōtō season, with pumpkin, taro and mushrooms. December and January bring the clearest days for seeing Fuji.

meibutsu.name: Hōtō
meibutsu.what: Thick noodles cooked in an iron pot in miso broth with pumpkin, vegetables and mushrooms.

meibutsu.name: Yoshida udon
meibutsu.what: Very firm udon with boiled cabbage, aburaage and meat (traditionally horse, cooked), seasoned with suridane, a chilli-and-sesame paste.
meibutsu.where: Miura Udon, 麺許皆伝, 桜井うどん in Fujiyoshida.

meibutsu.name: Pheasant
meibutsu.what: Pheasant in hōtō and other dishes, the speciality of a house more than 50 years old.

meibutsu.name: Shingen-mochi
meibutsu.what: Little mochi with kinako and black-sugar syrup, Yamanashi's classic souvenir.

meibutsu.name: Kōshū wine
meibutsu.what: Yamanashi is the capital of Japanese wine, made from the white Kōshū grape.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: Alcohol. Fernanda skips it and has local grape juice instead.

areas.name: Around Kawaguchiko Station
areas.story: Where the big hōtō halls and Kiji-tei are.
areas.tips: The hōtō halls (Fudō and others) sit at 3.41–3.49 on Tabelog: easy, not excellent.
areas.dec_jan: We're here 5–7 Jan, just after New Year; whether everything has reopened is to confirm.

areas.name: Central Fujiyoshida
areas.story: The old silk and pilgrim town, with dozens of udon shops.
areas.tips: Lunch only; many close on Sundays.
areas.dec_jan: Many close over New Year: check shop by shop that they've reopened by 5–7 Jan. None of our days is a Sunday.

places.name: Kiji-tei
places.area: Kawaguchiko · 10 min walk from the station
places.why: Tabelog's Yamanashi hōtō roundup puts this pheasant house at the top, above the tourist halls.
places.group: Private room for 10–20; seven fit if we book.
places.booking: Online, taken 9:00–10:00 on weekdays. Only 5 groups a day.
places.dec_jan: Lunch only; closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, so for us only Thu 7 Jan, our leaving day. Post-New Year hours to confirm.

places.name: Miura Udon
places.why: What people around Fuji really eat for lunch.
places.order: Hot udon with cabbage and meat, plus suridane.
places.group: 45 seats at tables of 6: ask to squeeze a seventh in, or split 4+3.
places.dec_jan: 10:00–14:00; closed Wednesdays (6 Jan), so Tue 5 or Thu 7 Jan. Post-New Year hours to confirm.
